newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Shenzhen shares end lower on holiday mood.
newsitem.headline: Shenzhen shares end lower on holiday mood.

text.p: Shenzhen's foreign currency B share market closed lower on Thursday, with wait-and-see sentiment prevailing ahead of the Hong Kong handover holiday, brokers said.
The B share index lost 0.73 points or 0.50 percent to 143.80 points as turnover shrank to HK$67 million from Wednesday's HK$77 million.

The domestic A share index slipped 3.12 points or 0.67 percent to 460.09 as new listings diverted some "hot money" from existing shares, brokers said. Turnover reached 9.4 billion yuan, compared with 9.2 billion yuan in the previous session.

"Investors are slicing their holdings before the holiday because they are concerned that Beijing might announce some negative market-moving news after the Hong Kong handover," an analyst with China Guotai Securities said.
The Shenzhen Stock Exchange has said it will close on June 30 and July 1 to mark the reversion to Chinese sovereignty of the British colony. Trading will resume on Wednesday, July 2.
There had been talk in the market that Beijing would introduce new measures in July to further counter stock speculation, brokers said.
"Some institutions have been pulling out of the market before the handover, which has for a long time served as an excuse for them to bolster share prices," Cheng Li, another Guotai analyst, said.
Many investors had thought Beijing would not take any market-cooling measures in the last few months before the handover.
But their hopes were dashed earlier this month when Beijing sacked the heads of some of the country's top brokerage companies, banks and listed firms for irregular stock trading.
"The handover will soon be history and the market is waiting for new trading incentive," Cheng said.
Shenzhen Petrochemical was the worst B share performer, falling HK$0.20 or 6.67 percent to HK$2.80.
Seven companies listed a combined 340 million A shares in Shenzhen on Thursday, a record number of new company listings on the south China bourse in one day, brokers said.
They all posted strong debuts, which attracted many investors seeking quick profits, they said.
New listings are not calculated into indices on their first day of trading.
Petrochemical concern Yueyang Xingchang was the weakest A share performer, sliding 3.48 yuan or 9.9 percent to 31.37 yuan.
Huludao Zinc Industry Co Ltd , the world's biggest zinc smelter, listed 90 million A shares in Shenzhen on Thursday and closed the session at 12.00 yuan against an issue price of 7.42 yuan.
Volume reached 53 million shares, making it the most actively traded counter.
